title.zh: 卷六十一 列傳第十一: 溫大雅 陳叔達 竇威
title.en: Volume 61 Biographies 11: Wen Daya, Chen Shuda, Dou Wei
title.raw: 卷六十一 列傳第十一: 溫大雅 陳叔達 竇威 Volume 61 Biographies 11: Wen Daya, Chen Shuda, Dou Wei

sentences.zh: 溫大雅 子無隱 大雅弟彥博 子振 挺 大雅弟大有

translations.literal: Wen Daya; son Wuyin; Daya's younger brother Yanbo; Yanbo's sons Zhen and Ting; Daya's younger brother Dayou.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Daya; his son Wuyin; Daya's younger brother Yanbo; Yanbo's sons Zhen and Ting; and Daya's younger brother Dayou.

sentences.zh: 陳叔達 竇威子惲 兄子軌 軌子奉節 琮 從子抗 抗子衍 靜 靜子逵 誕 誕子孝慈孝慈子希玠 誕少子孝諶 抗季弟璡

translations.literal: Chen Shuda; Dou Wei—his son Yun; nephew Gui; Gui's sons Fengjie and Cong; clansman Kang; Kang's sons Yan and Jing; Jing's son Kui; Dan; Dan's sons Xiaoci; Xiaoci's son Xijue; Dan's younger son Xiaochen; Kang's youngest younger brother Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shuda; Dou Wei—his son Yun; his nephew Gui; Gui's sons Fengjie and Cong; his clansman Kang; Kang's sons Yan and Jing; Jing's son Kui; Dan; Dan's son Xiaoci, whose son was Xijue; Dan's younger son Xiaochen; and Kang's youngest younger brother Jin.

sentences.zh: 溫大雅，字彥弘，太原祁人也。

translations.literal: Wen Daya, courtesy name Yanhong, was a native of Qi in Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Daya, whose courtesy name was Yanhong, came from Qi in Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 父君悠，北齊文林館學士，隋泗州司馬。

translations.literal: His father Junyou was a scholar of the Northern Qi Forest of Literature, and under the Sui served as marshal of Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Junyou had been a scholar in the Northern Qi's Forest of Literature and later served the Sui as marshal of Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 大業末，為司隸從事，見隋政日亂，謝病而歸。

translations.literal: At the end of the Daye era he served as an aide in the Metropolitan Office; seeing Sui government daily more chaotic, he pleaded illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Daye reign he held a post in the metropolitan administration, but as he watched the Sui order unravel day by day he pleaded illness and withdrew to his home.

sentences.zh: 大雅性至孝，少好學，以才辯知名。

translations.literal: Daya was by nature profoundly filial; in youth he loved learning and was known for talent and eloquence.
translations.idiomatic: Daya was deeply filial by nature. As a youth he loved study and won renown for his talent and eloquence.

sentences.zh: 仕隋東宮學士、長安縣尉，以父憂去職。

translations.literal: He served the Sui as a scholar in the Eastern Palace and as magistrate of Chang'an County, then left office on his father's death.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Sui he served as a scholar in the crown prince's palace and as magistrate of Chang'an County, then left office to mourn his father.

sentences.zh: 後以天下方亂，不求仕進。

translations.literal: Later, because the realm was in turmoil, he sought no further advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward, with the empire falling into chaos, he made no effort to resume his career.

sentences.zh: 高祖鎮太原，甚禮之。

translations.literal: When Gaozu was stationed at Taiyuan he treated Daya with great courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu was posted to Taiyuan he treated Daya with marked respect.

sentences.zh: 義兵起，引為大將軍府記室參軍，專掌文翰。

translations.literal: When the righteous army rose, Daya was brought in as recorder of the Grand General's headquarters and charged solely with documents.
translations.idiomatic: When the uprising began, Daya was appointed recorder on the Grand General's staff and put in sole charge of written communications.

sentences.zh: 禪代之際，與司錄竇威、主簿陳叔達參定禮儀。

translations.literal: At the time of the abdication and succession, together with Registrar Dou Wei and Chief Clerk Chen Shuda he helped fix the ritual protocols.
translations.idiomatic: At the transfer of the mandate he worked with Registrar Dou Wei and Chief Clerk Chen Shuda to settle the court rituals.

sentences.zh: 武德元年，歷遷黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wude he was promoted in succession to Vice Minister of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Wude he rose through successive posts to Vice Minister of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 弟彥博，為中書侍郎；

translations.literal: His younger brother Yanbo served as Vice Minister of the Secretariat;
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Yanbo served as Vice Minister of the Secretariat;

sentences.zh: 對居近密，議者榮之。

translations.literal: the two held neighboring posts close to the throne, and commentators regarded this as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: the two held neighboring posts close to the throne, and observers spoke of the family with admiration.

sentences.zh: 高祖從容謂曰：「我起義晉陽，為卿一門耳。」

translations.literal: Gaozu said to him at ease, "When I raised the righteous army at Jinyang, it was for your whole clan."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said to him in an easy tone, "When I raised the army at Jinyang, I did it for your whole household."

sentences.zh: 尋轉工部，進拜陝東道大行台工部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was transferred to the Ministry of Works and advanced to Minister of Works on the Shandong Grand Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was moved to the Ministry of Works and then promoted to Minister of Works on the Eastern Shaanxi Grand Commission.

sentences.zh: 太宗以隱太子、巢刺王之故，令大雅鎮洛陽以俟變。

translations.literal: Because of the Hidden Crown Prince and the Prince of Chao and Assassin, Taizong had Daya garrison Luoyang to await developments.
translations.idiomatic: On account of the struggle involving the Hidden Crown Prince and the Prince of Chao and Assassin, Taizong stationed Daya at Luoyang to watch for any turn of events.

sentences.zh: 大雅數陳秘策，甚蒙嘉賞。

translations.literal: Daya repeatedly set forth secret stratagems and won high praise.
translations.idiomatic: Daya repeatedly offered confidential counsel and won high praise for it.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，累轉禮部尚書，封黎國公。

translations.literal: When Taizong took the throne, Daya was promoted in succession to Minister of Rites and enfeoffed as Duke of Li.
translations.idiomatic: After Taizong's accession, Daya rose through successive posts to Minister of Rites and was enfeoffed as Duke of Li.

sentences.zh: 大雅將改葬其祖父，筮者曰：「葬於此地，害兄而福弟。」

translations.literal: When Daya was about to rebury his grandfather, the diviner said, "If buried in this place, it will harm the elder brother and bless the younger."
translations.idiomatic: When Daya was preparing to rebury his grandfather, the diviner said, "If you bury him in this spot, it will harm the elder brother and bless the younger."

sentences.zh: 大雅曰：「若得家弟永康，我將含笑入地。」

translations.literal: Daya said, "If my younger brother at home may enjoy lasting peace, I shall go to my grave with a smile."
translations.idiomatic: Daya replied, "If my younger brother may live out his days in peace, I shall go to my grave with a smile."

sentences.zh: 葬訖，歲余而卒，謚曰孝。

translations.literal: After the burial was complete, a little more than a year later he died; his posthumous title was Filial.
translations.idiomatic: The burial was carried out, and a little more than a year later he died. His posthumous title was Filial.

sentences.zh: 撰《創業起居注》三卷。

translations.literal: He compiled three fascicles of 《Records of the Founding Court》.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote three fascicles of 《Records of the Founding Court》.

sentences.zh: 永徽五年，贈尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yonghui he was posthumously made Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Yonghui he was posthumously appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 子無隱，官至工部侍郎。

translations.literal: His son Wuyin rose to Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wuyin rose to the post of Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 大雅弟彥博。

translations.literal: Daya's younger brother Yanbo.
translations.idiomatic: Daya's younger brother was Yanbo.

sentences.zh: 彥博幼聰悟，有口辯，涉獵書記。

translations.literal: Yanbo was clever and perceptive in youth, possessed eloquence, and ranged widely through written records.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo was clever and quick-witted as a boy, gifted with eloquence, and read widely in books and documents.

sentences.zh: 初，其父友薛道衡、李綱常見彥博兄弟三人，咸嘆異曰：「皆卿相才也。」

translations.literal: Earlier, his father's friends Xue Daoheng and Li Gang often saw Yanbo and his two brothers and all marveled, saying, "Each is material for minister and chancellor."
translations.idiomatic: In earlier days his father's friends Xue Daoheng and Li Gang would often see Yanbo and his two brothers and marvel, saying, "Every one of them has the makings of a minister or chancellor."

sentences.zh: 開皇末，為州牧秦孝王俊所薦，授文林郎，直內史省，轉通直謁者。

translations.literal: Near the end of Kaihuang he was recommended by the prefectural governor Prince Qin Xiaojun and appointed Gentleman of the Forest of Literature, serving in the Secretariat, then transferred to Direct Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Near the close of Kaihuang he was recommended by the prefectural governor Prince Qin Xiaojun, appointed Gentleman of the Forest of Literature, assigned to the Secretariat, and later transferred to Direct Attendant.

sentences.zh: 及隋亂，幽州總管羅藝引為司馬。

translations.literal: When the Sui fell into disorder, the regional commander of Youzhou, Luo Yi, brought him in as marshal.
translations.idiomatic: When the Sui order collapsed, Luo Yi, regional commander of Youzhou, took him on as marshal.

sentences.zh: 藝以幽州歸國，彥博贊成其事，授幽州總管府長史。

translations.literal: When Yi submitted Youzhou to the new state, Yanbo helped bring the matter about and was appointed chief clerk of the Youzhou headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi surrendered Youzhou to the Tang cause, Yanbo helped bring it about and was made chief clerk of the Youzhou headquarters.

sentences.zh: 未幾，征為中書舍人，俄遷中書侍郎，封西河郡公。

translations.literal: Before long he was summoned as Drafting Secretary, soon promoted to Vice Minister of the Secretariat, and enfeoffed as Duke of Xihe commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was called to court as Drafting Secretary, soon promoted to Vice Minister of the Secretariat, and enfeoffed as Duke of Xihe.

sentences.zh: 時高麗遣使貢方物，高祖謂群臣曰：「名實之間，理須相副。

translations.literal: At that time Goguryeo sent envoys bearing tribute; Gaozu told the assembled ministers, "Between name and reality there must be a proper correspondence.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Goguryeo sent envoys with tribute gifts, and Gaozu told the assembled ministers, "Between title and reality there ought to be a proper match.

sentences.zh: 高麗稱臣於隋，終拒煬帝，此亦何臣之有？

translations.literal: Goguryeo called itself a vassal of the Sui yet in the end defied Emperor Yang—what sort of vassalage is this?
translations.idiomatic: Goguryeo called itself a vassal of the Sui, yet in the end it defied Emperor Yang—what kind of vassalage is that?

sentences.zh: 朕敬於萬物，不欲驕貴，但據土宇，務共安人，何必令其稱臣以自尊大？

translations.literal: I respect all things and do not wish to grow proud and lofty; I hold only the realm and strive with all to bring peace to the people—why must I make them call themselves vassals to aggrandize myself?
translations.idiomatic: I hold all things in respect and do not wish to grow proud; I hold the realm only to bring peace to the people—why must I make them call themselves vassals merely to puff myself up?

sentences.zh: 可即為詔，述朕此懷也。」

translations.literal: You may at once draft an edict stating this intent of mine."
translations.idiomatic: Draft an edict at once and set forth this intent of mine."

sentences.zh: 彥博進曰：「遼東之地，周為箕子之國，漢家之玄菟郡耳。

translations.literal: Yanbo advanced and said, "The lands of Liaodong were in Zhou the state of Jizi, and under the Han merely the commandery of Xuantu.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo stepped forward and said, "The lands of Liaodong were in Zhou the domain of Jizi, and under the Han no more than the commandery of Xuantu.

sentences.zh: 魏、晉已前，近在提封之內，不可許以不臣。

translations.literal: Before Wei and Jin they lay within our very frontier—one cannot allow them not to be vassals.
translations.idiomatic: Before Wei and Jin they lay within our very frontier; we cannot allow them to stand as our equals.

sentences.zh: 若與高麗抗禮，則四夷何以瞻仰？

translations.literal: If we treat Goguryeo as an equal in ritual, how will the four barbarians look up to us?
translations.idiomatic: If we treat Goguryeo as an equal in ritual, how will the four quarters of barbarians look to us?

sentences.zh: 且中國之於夷狄，猶太陽之比列星，理無降尊，俯同夷貊。」

translations.literal: Moreover, China toward the barbarians is like the sun toward the lesser stars—by right there is no lowering of dignity to bow with the Yi and Mo."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, China's relation to the barbarians is like the sun's to the lesser stars—by right there is no lowering of dignity to stoop to their level."

sentences.zh: 高祖乃止。

translations.literal: Gaozu thereupon desisted.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu thereupon dropped the plan.

sentences.zh: 其年，突厥入寇，命右衛大將軍張瑾為并州道行軍總管，出拒之，以彥博為行軍長史。

translations.literal: That year the Turks invaded; he ordered Grand General of the Right Guards Zhang Jin as Grand Commander of the Bingzhou Expedition to go out and resist them, with Yanbo as expedition chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Turks raided the borders. Gaozu appointed Grand General of the Right Guards Zhang Jin Grand Commander of the Bingzhou Expedition to march out against them, with Yanbo as expedition chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 與虜戰於太谷，軍敗，彥博沒於虜庭。

translations.literal: They fought the enemy at Taigu; the army was defeated and Yanbo was lost in the Turk camp.
translations.idiomatic: They met the enemy at Taigu; the army was defeated and Yanbo fell into Turk hands.

sentences.zh: 突厥以其近臣，苦問以國家虛實及兵馬多少，彥博固不肯言。

translations.literal: The Turks, because he was a close minister, pressed him hard on the state's strength and weakness and the numbers of troops and horses; Yanbo steadfastly refused to speak.
translations.idiomatic: Because he was a close minister of the court, the Turks pressed him relentlessly about the empire's strength and the size of its armies; Yanbo steadfastly refused to answer.

sentences.zh: 頡利怒，遷於陰山苦塞之地。

translations.literal: Khan Jiali grew angry and moved him to the bitter passes of the Yin Mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Khan Jiali flew into a rage and had him moved to the harsh passes of the Yin Mountains.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，突厥送款，始征彥博還朝，授雍州治中，尋檢校吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Taizong took the throne the Turks sent pledges of submission; only then was Yanbo summoned back to court, appointed Administrator of Yongzhou, and soon made acting Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: After Taizong's accession the Turks offered submission, and only then was Yanbo summoned back to court, appointed Administrator of Yongzhou, and soon made acting Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 彥博意有沙汰，多所損抑，而退者不伏，囂訟盈庭。

translations.literal: Yanbo intended a purge and cut down many; those removed would not submit, and clamorous suits filled the court.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo set out to purge the ranks and demoted many officials; those removed refused to accept it, and the court rang with their noisy appeals.

sentences.zh: 彥博惟騁辭辯，與之相詰，終日喧擾，頗為識者所嗤。

translations.literal: Yanbo relied only on unleashing his eloquence and arguing with them; the uproar lasted all day, and men of discernment largely scoffed at him.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo could only unleash his eloquence and argue them down; the hall was in uproar all day, and thoughtful observers largely scoffed at the spectacle.

sentences.zh: 復拜中書侍郎，兼太子右庶子。

translations.literal: He was again appointed Vice Minister of the Secretariat and concurrently Right Vice Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was again appointed Vice Minister of the Secretariat and concurrently Right Vice Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 貞觀二年，遷御史大夫，仍檢校中書侍郎事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenguan he was transferred to Censor-in-Chief while still acting in the affairs of Vice Minister of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhenguan he was made Censor-in-Chief while continuing to handle the duties of Vice Minister of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 彥博善於宣吐，每奉使入朝，詔問四方風俗，承受綸言，有若成誦。

translations.literal: Yanbo excelled at public declamation; whenever he came to court on mission and was questioned by edict on the customs of the four quarters, he received the imperial words as though they were already memorized.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo excelled at public speech. Whenever he came to court on embassy and was questioned by edict about customs throughout the realm, he received the imperial words as though he had memorized them beforehand.

sentences.zh: 聲韻高朗，響溢殿庭，進止雍容，觀者拭目。

translations.literal: His tone was high and clear, his voice overflowing the hall; his bearing in advancing and withdrawing was composed, and onlookers wiped their eyes.
translations.idiomatic: His voice rang high and clear, filling the hall; his bearing as he advanced and withdrew was composed, and onlookers watched in wonder.

sentences.zh: 四年，遷中書令，進爵虞國公。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was transferred to Secretariat Director and advanced in rank to Duke of the State of Yu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was made Secretariat Director and advanced in rank to Duke of Yu.

sentences.zh: 高祖常宴朝臣，詔太宗諭旨，既而顧謂近臣曰：「何如溫彥博？」

translations.literal: Gaozu often feasted the court ministers and ordered Taizong to convey the imperial intent; then he turned to his close attendants and said, "How does he compare with Wen Yanbo?"
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu often feasted the court ministers and had Taizong convey the imperial message; then he turned to his close attendants and said, "How does he compare with Wen Yanbo?"

sentences.zh: 其見重如此。

translations.literal: Such was the esteem in which he was held.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the esteem in which he was held.

sentences.zh: 初，突厥之降也，詔議安邊之術。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Turks submitted, an edict called for discussion of methods to secure the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the Turks submitted, the court was ordered to debate how best to secure the frontier.

sentences.zh: 朝士多言：「突厥恃強，擾亂中國，為日久矣。

translations.literal: Many at court said, "The Turks have relied on their strength and troubled China for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Many at court argued, "The Turks have long relied on their strength to harass China.

sentences.zh: 今天實喪之，窮來歸我，本非慕義之心也。

translations.literal: Now Heaven has truly abandoned them; in destitution they come to submit to us—this is not a heart that admires righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Now Heaven has truly abandoned them; in their desperation they come to submit to us—this is not born of admiration for our virtue.

sentences.zh: 因其歸命，分其種落，俘之河南，散屬州縣，各使耕田，變其風俗。

translations.literal: Taking advantage of their submission, divide their tribes, take them captive south of the Yellow River, scatter them among prefectures and counties, set each to till the fields, and change their customs.
translations.idiomatic: Let us take advantage of their submission, break up their tribes, move them south of the Yellow River, scatter them among the prefectures and counties, set them to farming, and change their ways.

sentences.zh: 百萬胡虜，可得化而為漢，則中國有加戶之利，塞北常空矣。」

translations.literal: A million barbarian captives could be transformed into Han; then China would gain households, and the northern frontier would stand forever empty."
translations.idiomatic: A million barbarian captives could be transformed into Han subjects; China would gain households, and the northern marches would stand forever empty."

sentences.zh: 惟彥博議曰：「漢建武時，置降匈奴於五原塞下，全其部落，得為捍蔽，又不離其土俗，因而撫之。

translations.literal: Only Yanbo argued, "In the Jianwu era of Han, surrendered Xiongnu were settled below the passes of Wuyuan; their tribes were kept whole so they could serve as a shield, yet without leaving their native customs, and thus they were comforted.
translations.idiomatic: Only Yanbo argued, "In the Jianwu era of Han, surrendered Xiongnu were settled below the passes of Wuyuan; their tribes were kept intact so they could serve as a shield, yet without being torn from their native customs, and thus they were won over.

sentences.zh: 一則實空虛之地，二則示無猜之心。

translations.literal: First, it truly emptied the vacant lands; second, it showed a heart free of suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: That plan truly filled empty lands, and it showed a heart free of suspicion.

sentences.zh: 若遣向西南，則乖物性，故非含育之道也。」

translations.literal: If we send them toward the southwest, we go against their nature—this is not the way of cherishing and nurturing."
translations.idiomatic: If we send them toward the southwest, we go against their nature; that is not the way of cherishing and nurturing subjects."

sentences.zh: 太宗從之，遂處降人於朔方之地，其入居長安者近且萬家。

translations.literal: Taizong followed this view and thereupon settled the submitted people in the Shuofang region; those who entered and dwelt in Chang'an approached ten thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong followed his counsel and settled the submitted Turks in the Shuofang region; those who took up residence in Chang'an approached ten thousand households.

sentences.zh: 議者尤為不便，欲建突厥國於河外。

translations.literal: The debaters found this especially inconvenient and wished to establish a Turk state beyond the river.
translations.idiomatic: Critics found the arrangement especially troubling and wished to establish a Turk state beyond the river.

sentences.zh: 彥博又執奏曰：「既已納之，無故遣去，深為可惜。」

translations.literal: Yanbo again pressed his memorial, saying, "Since we have already taken them in, to send them away without cause would be deeply regrettable."
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo again pressed his memorial, saying, "Since we have already taken them in, to send them away without cause would be a great waste."

sentences.zh: 與魏徵等爭論，數年不決。

translations.literal: He debated with Wei Zheng and others, and for several years no decision was reached.
translations.idiomatic: He debated with Wei Zheng and others, and for several years no final decision was reached.

sentences.zh: 十年，遷尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was transferred to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 明年薨，年六十四。

translations.literal: The next year he died, aged sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he died, at the age of sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 彥博自掌知機務，即杜絕賓客，國之利害，知無不言，太宗以是嘉之。

translations.literal: From the time Yanbo took charge of confidential affairs he cut off visitors; whatever harmed or benefited the state, he spoke of without reserve, and Taizong for this praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yanbo took charge of confidential affairs he cut off visitors entirely; whatever harmed or benefited the state, he spoke of without reserve, and Taizong praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 及薨，謂侍臣曰：「彥博以憂國之故，勞精竭神，我見其不逮，已二年矣。

translations.literal: When he died, he told his attendants, "Yanbo, for the sake of caring for the state, exhausted his spirit and strength; I saw him failing for two years already.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, Taizong told his attendants, "Yanbo wore himself out caring for the state; I saw him failing for two years already.

sentences.zh: 恨不縱其閒逸，致夭性靈。」

translations.literal: I regret that I did not let him enjoy leisure and thereby cut short his vital nature."
translations.idiomatic: I regret that I did not let him enjoy some leisure and thereby cut short his life."

sentences.zh: 彥博家無正寢，及卒之日，殯於別室，太宗命有司為造堂焉。

translations.literal: Yanbo's household had no proper main chamber; on the day of his death the coffin was placed in a side room, and Taizong ordered the relevant offices to build a hall for him.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo's household had no proper main hall; on the day of his death the coffin lay in a side room, and Taizong ordered the relevant offices to build a hall for the family.

sentences.zh: 贈特進，謚曰恭，陪葬昭陵。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Special Advancement; his posthumous title was Respectful, and he was buried with honor at Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed Special Advancement; his posthumous title was Respectful, and he was buried with honor at Zhaoling.

sentences.zh: 子振，少有雅望，官至太子舍人，居喪以毀卒。

translations.literal: His son Zhen in youth had an elegant reputation; he rose to Crown Prince Attendant and died from grief in mourning.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhen enjoyed an elegant reputation in youth, rose to Crown Prince Attendant, and died from grief during mourning.

sentences.zh: 振弟挺，尚高祖女千金公主，官至延州刺史。

translations.literal: Zhen's younger brother Ting married Gaozu's daughter Princess Qianjin and rose to Prefect of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen's younger brother Ting married Gaozu's daughter Princess Qianjin and rose to the post of Prefect of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 大雅弟大有，字彥將，性端謹，少以學行稱。

translations.literal: Daya's younger brother Dayou, courtesy name Yanjiang, was by nature upright and careful; in youth he was known for learning and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Daya's younger brother Dayou, whose courtesy name was Yanjiang, was upright and careful by nature and was known in youth for his learning and conduct.

sentences.zh: 隋仁壽中，尚書右丞李綱表薦之，授羽騎尉。

translations.literal: In the Renshou era of the Sui, Right Vice Director Li Gang memorialized recommending him, and he was appointed Captain of Feathered Riders.
translations.idiomatic: During the Renshou era of the Sui, Right Vice Director Li Gang recommended him by memorial, and he was appointed Captain of Feathered Riders.

sentences.zh: 尋丁憂去，職歸鄉里。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he left on mourning for his father and returned to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he left office to mourn his father and returned to his home district.

sentences.zh: 義旗初舉，高祖引為太原令。

translations.literal: When the righteous banner was first raised, Gaozu brought him in as magistrate of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When the uprising first began, Gaozu appointed him magistrate of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 從太宗擊西河，高祖謂曰：「士馬尚少，要資經略，以卿參謀軍事，其善建功名也！

translations.literal: Following Taizong in the attack on Xihe, Gaozu said to him, "Our troops and horses are still few; we need planning and strategy—take this post to advise on military affairs and build your merit well!
translations.idiomatic: When he followed Taizong in the attack on Xihe, Gaozu told him, "Our forces are still few; we need strategy—take this post to advise on military affairs and win your merit there!

sentences.zh: 事之成敗，當以此行卜之。

translations.literal: Whether the affair succeeds or fails should be divined by this campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Whether our cause succeeds or fails may be read from this campaign.

sentences.zh: 若克西河，帝業成矣。」

translations.literal: If Xihe is taken, the imperial enterprise is accomplished."
translations.idiomatic: If we take Xihe, the imperial enterprise is assured."

sentences.zh: 及破西河而還，復以本官攝大將軍府記室，與兄大雅共掌機密。

translations.literal: When Xihe was taken and they returned, he again held his former office in an acting capacity as recorder of the Grand General's headquarters, sharing confidential affairs with his elder brother Daya.
translations.idiomatic: When Xihe fell and they returned, he again served in his former post as acting recorder on the Grand General's staff, sharing confidential affairs with his elder brother Daya.

sentences.zh: 大有以昆季同在機務，意不自安，固請他職。

translations.literal: Dayou, because brothers together held confidential posts, felt ill at ease and firmly requested another office.
translations.idiomatic: Because he and his brothers together held posts in confidential affairs, Dayou felt ill at ease and firmly asked for another assignment.

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「我虛心相待，不以為疑，卿何自疑也？」

translations.literal: Gaozu said, "I receive you with an open heart and do not regard you with suspicion—why do you suspect yourself?"
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said, "I deal with you in good faith and harbor no suspicion—why do you doubt yourself?"

sentences.zh: 大有雖應命，然每退讓，遠避機權，僚列以此多之。

translations.literal: Dayou though he accepted the command yet each time yielded ground, keeping far from the levers of power; his colleagues for this praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Dayou accepted the order, yet each time he yielded ground and kept his distance from power; his colleagues admired him for it.

sentences.zh: 武德元年，累轉中書侍郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wude he was promoted in succession to Vice Minister of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Wude he rose through successive posts to Vice Minister of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 會卒，高祖甚傷惜之，贈鴻臚卿。

translations.literal: He happened to die; Gaozu grieved deeply for him and posthumously made him Director of the Court for Diplomatic Reception.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon afterward; Gaozu grieved deeply for him and posthumously appointed him Director of the Court for Diplomatic Reception.

sentences.zh: 初，大雅在隋，與顏思魯俱在東宮，彥博與思魯弟愍楚同直內史省，彥將與愍楚弟游秦典校秘閣。

translations.literal: Earlier, Daya under the Sui was together with Yan Silu in the Eastern Palace; Yanbo was together with Silu's younger brother Minchu on duty in the Secretariat; Yanjiang together with Minchu's younger brother Youqin oversaw the collation of the Secret Archive.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, under the Sui, Daya had served in the Eastern Palace together with Yan Silu; Yanbo had served in the Secretariat together with Silu's younger brother Minchu; and Yanjiang had overseen the Secret Archive together with Minchu's younger brother Youqin.

sentences.zh: 二家兄弟，各為一時人物之選。

translations.literal: The brothers of the two families were each chosen men of their age.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers of the two families were each among the leading men of their day.

sentences.zh: 少時學業，顏氏為優；

translations.literal: In youth for scholarly achievement the Yan clan was superior;
translations.idiomatic: In youth the Yan clan had the edge in scholarly achievement;

sentences.zh: 其後職位，溫氏為盛。

translations.literal: afterward in office the Wen clan was flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: but afterward in office the Wen clan stood in the ascendant.

sentences.zh: 陳叔達，字子聰，陳宣帝第十六子也。

translations.literal: Chen Shuda, courtesy name Zicong, was the sixteenth son of Emperor Xuan of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shuda, whose courtesy name was Zicong, was the sixteenth son of Emperor Xuan of Chen.

sentences.zh: 善容止，頗有才學，在陳封義陽王。

translations.literal: He was skilled in bearing and deportment, possessed considerable learning, and under Chen was enfeoffed as Prince of Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was graceful in bearing and well learned; under the Chen he was enfeoffed as Prince of Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 年十餘歲，嘗侍宴，賦詩十韻，援筆便就，僕射徐陵甚奇之。

translations.literal: When he was just over ten he once attended a feast, composed a poem in ten rhymes, took up the brush and finished at once; Vice Director Xu Ling marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: When he was barely past ten he once attended a feast and composed a ten-rhyme poem at a stroke; Vice Director Xu Ling marveled at him.

sentences.zh: 歷侍中、丹陽尹、都官尚書。

translations.literal: He served in succession as Attendant-in-Ordinary, Intendant of Danyang, and Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He served in succession as Attendant-in-Ordinary, Intendant of Danyang, and Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 入隋，久不得調。

translations.literal: After entering the Sui he long received no appointment.
translations.idiomatic: After the Chen fell he entered Sui service but long received no appointment.

sentences.zh: 大業中，拜內史舍人，出為絳郡通守。

translations.literal: In the Daye era he was appointed Drafting Secretary and sent out as Communications Prefect of Jiang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daye reign he was appointed Drafting Secretary and then sent out as Communications Prefect of Jiang commandery.

sentences.zh: 義師至絳郡，叔達以郡歸款，授丞相府主簿，封漢東郡公。

translations.literal: When the righteous army reached Jiang commandery, Shuda submitted the commandery and was appointed Chief Clerk of the Chancellor's headquarters and enfeoffed as Duke of Handong commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When the uprising reached Jiang commandery, Shuda surrendered the district and was appointed Chief Clerk on the Chancellor's staff and enfeoffed as Duke of Handong.

sentences.zh: 與記室溫大雅同掌機密，軍書、赦令及禪代文誥，多叔達所為。

translations.literal: Together with Recorder Wen Daya he shared confidential affairs; military documents, amnesties, and the proclamations of the abdication and succession were largely Shuda's work.
translations.idiomatic: He shared confidential affairs with Recorder Wen Daya; military documents, amnesties, and the proclamations of the abdication and succession were largely his work.

sentences.zh: 武德元年，授黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wude he was appointed Vice Minister of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Wude he was appointed Vice Minister of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 二年，兼納言。

translations.literal: In the second year he was made concurrent Remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was made concurrent Remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 四年，拜侍中。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 叔達明辯，善容止，每有敷奏，搢紳莫不屬目。

translations.literal: Shuda was clear in argument and skilled in bearing; whenever he presented memorials, the gentry all fixed their eyes on him.
translations.idiomatic: Shuda was sharp in debate and graceful in bearing; whenever he addressed the throne, the court looked to him.

sentences.zh: 江南名士薄游長安者，多為薦拔。

translations.literal: Famous scholars of the south who briefly traveled to Chang'an were largely recommended and promoted by him.
translations.idiomatic: Many renowned scholars from the south who passed through Chang'an won his recommendation and promotion.

sentences.zh: 五年，進封江國公。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of the State of Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was advanced in rank to Duke of Jiang.

sentences.zh: 嘗賜食於御前，得蒲萄，執而不食。

translations.literal: He was once granted food before the throne and received grapes, which he held but did not eat.
translations.idiomatic: Once, when he was granted food before the throne, he received grapes but held them without eating.

sentences.zh: 高祖問其故，對曰：「臣母患口乾，求之不能致，欲歸以遺母。」

translations.literal: Gaozu asked the reason; he replied, "My mother suffers from dry mouth; I could not obtain these though I sought them, and wish to take them home as a gift for her."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu asked why; he replied, "My mother suffers from dry mouth. I could not obtain grapes though I sought them, and I wish to take these home for her."

sentences.zh: 高祖喟然流涕曰：「卿有母遺乎！」

translations.literal: Gaozu sighed with tears and said, "You still have a mother to provide for!"
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu sighed with tears and said, "You still have a mother to care for!"

sentences.zh: 因賜物三百段。

translations.literal: Thereupon he bestowed three hundred bolts of goods.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he bestowed three hundred bolts of goods on him.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，加授光祿大夫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan he was additionally appointed Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Zhenguan he was additionally appointed Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 尋坐與蕭瑀對御忿爭免官。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was removed from office for quarreling angrily with Xiao Yu before the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was dismissed for quarreling angrily with Xiao Yu before the throne.

sentences.zh: 未幾，丁母憂。

translations.literal: Before long he entered mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he entered mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 叔達先有疾，太宗慮其危殆，遣使禁絕吊賓。

translations.literal: Shuda had long been ill; Taizong feared he was in peril and sent envoys to forbid condolence visitors.
translations.idiomatic: Shuda had long been ill; Taizong feared for his life and sent envoys to forbid condolence visitors.

sentences.zh: 服闋，授遂州都督，以疾不行。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was appointed Regional Commander of Suizhou but did not take up the post because of illness.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he was appointed Regional Commander of Suizhou but did not take up the post because of illness.

sentences.zh: 久之，拜禮部尚書。

translations.literal: After a long interval he was appointed Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was appointed Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 建成、元吉嫉害太宗，陰行譖毀，高祖惑其言，將有貶責，叔達固諫乃止。

translations.literal: Jiancheng and Yuanji envied and harmed Taizong, secretly slandering him; Gaozu was swayed by their words and was about to demote and rebuke Taizong, but Shuda firmly remonstrated and stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: Jiancheng and Yuanji envied Taizong and secretly slandered him; Gaozu was swayed by their words and was about to punish Taizong, but Shuda firmly remonstrated and stopped it.

sentences.zh: 至是太宗勞之曰：「武德時，危難潛構，知公有讜言，今之此拜，有以相答。」

translations.literal: At this time Taizong thanked him, saying, "In the Wude era peril was secretly building; I know you spoke forthright counsel—this present appointment is my answer."
translations.idiomatic: At this time Taizong thanked him, saying, "In the Wude era peril was secretly building; I know you spoke forthright counsel—this appointment is my answer."

sentences.zh: 叔達謝曰：「此不獨為陛下，社稷計耳。」

translations.literal: Shuda declined, saying, "This was not only for Your Majesty but for the sake of the altars of state."
translations.idiomatic: Shuda declined, saying, "I did this not only for Your Majesty but for the sake of the realm."

sentences.zh: 後坐閨庭不理，為憲司所劾。

translations.literal: Later he was impeached by the censorate for neglecting his household affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Later the censorate impeached him for neglecting his household affairs.

sentences.zh: 朝廷惜其名臣，不欲彰其罪，聽以散秩歸第。

translations.literal: The court valued this famous minister and did not wish to expose his offense, allowing him to return home on an honorary stipend.
translations.idiomatic: The court valued this famous minister and did not wish to expose his offense, allowing him to return home on an honorary stipend.

sentences.zh: 九年卒，謚曰繆。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he died; his posthumous title was Erring.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he died; his posthumous title was Erring.

sentences.zh: 後贈戶部尚書，改謚曰忠。

translations.literal: Later he was posthumously made Minister of Revenue and his posthumous title was changed to Loyal.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was posthumously appointed Minister of Revenue and his posthumous title was changed to Loyal.

sentences.zh: 有集十五卷。

translations.literal: He left a collected works in fifteen fascicles.
translations.idiomatic: He left collected works in fifteen fascicles.

sentences.zh: 竇威，字文蔚，扶風平陸人，太穆皇后從父兄也。

translations.literal: Dou Wei, courtesy name Wenwei, was a native of Pinglu in Fufeng and a cousin on his father's side to Empress Taimu.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Wei, whose courtesy name was Wenwei, came from Pinglu in Fufeng and was a paternal cousin of Empress Taimu.

sentences.zh: 父熾，隋太傅。

translations.literal: His father Chi served the Sui as Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chi had served the Sui as Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 威家世勳貴，諸昆弟並尚武藝，而威耽玩文史，介然自守。

translations.literal: Wei's family for generations had been meritorious and noble; all his brothers prized martial arts, while Wei immersed himself in letters and history and kept himself aloof.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's family had been noble for generations; all his brothers prized martial arts, while Wei immersed himself in letters and history and held himself apart.

sentences.zh: 諸兄哂之，謂為「書痴」。

translations.literal: His elder brothers mocked him and called him a "book fool."
translations.idiomatic: His elder brothers mocked him and called him a "book fool."

sentences.zh: 隋內史令李德林舉秀異，射策甲科，拜秘書郎。

translations.literal: The Sui Secretariat Director Li Delin recommended him as outstanding; in the archery examination he took first class and was appointed Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Li Delin, Secretariat Director under the Sui, recommended him as outstanding; he took first class in the examination and was appointed Secretary.

sentences.zh: 秩滿當遷，而固守不調，在秘書十餘歲，其學業益廣。

translations.literal: When his term ended he should have been transferred, but he firmly refused reassignment; he remained in the Secretariat for more than ten years and his learning grew ever broader.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended he should have been transferred, but he firmly refused reassignment; he remained in the Secretariat for more than ten years and his learning grew ever broader.

sentences.zh: 時諸兄並以軍功致仕通顯，交結豪貴，賓客盈門，而威職掌閒散。

translations.literal: At that time all his brothers through military merit reached prominent office, formed ties with the powerful and noble, and filled their gates with guests, while Wei held a post that was idle and obscure.
translations.idiomatic: At that time all his brothers had risen to prominence through military merit, cultivated ties with the powerful, and filled their gates with guests, while Wei held an idle and obscure post.

sentences.zh: 諸兄更謂威曰：「昔孔子積學成聖，猶狼狽當時，棲遲若此，汝效此道，復欲何求？

translations.literal: His brothers again said to Wei, "In antiquity Confucius through accumulated learning became a sage, yet was still in straits in his own time and delayed like this—if you follow this path, what more do you seek?
translations.idiomatic: His brothers again said to Wei, "Confucius became a sage through accumulated learning, yet was still in straits in his own day and delayed like this—if you follow this path, what more do you seek?

sentences.zh: 名位不達，固其宜矣。」

translations.literal: That fame and office do not reach you is only fitting."
translations.idiomatic: That fame and office do not reach you is only fitting."

sentences.zh: 威笑而不答。

translations.literal: Wei smiled and did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Wei smiled and did not reply.

sentences.zh: 久之，蜀王秀闢為記室，以秀行事多不法，稱疾還田裡。

translations.literal: After a long interval Prince of Shu Xiu summoned him as recorder; because Xiu's conduct was often unlawful, Wei pleaded illness and returned to his fields.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval Prince of Shu Xiu summoned him as recorder; because Xiu's conduct was often unlawful, Wei pleaded illness and returned to his fields.

sentences.zh: 及秀廢黜，府僚多獲罪，唯威以先見保全。

translations.literal: When Xiu was deposed and removed, many staff members were punished; only Wei, through foresight, was preserved.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiu was deposed, many of his staff were punished; only Wei, through foresight, was spared.

sentences.zh: 大業四年，累遷內史舍人，以數陳得失忤旨，轉考功郎中，後坐事免，歸京師。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Daye he was promoted in succession to Drafting Secretary; because he repeatedly stated gains and losses and offended the imperial will, he was transferred to Director in the Bureau of Evaluations, later dismissed for an offense, and returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Daye he rose to Drafting Secretary; because he repeatedly stated what was right and wrong and offended the throne, he was transferred to Director in the Bureau of Evaluations, later dismissed for an offense, and returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 高祖入關，召補大丞相府司錄參軍。

translations.literal: When Gaozu entered the passes he was summoned to fill the post of Registrar of the Grand Chancellor's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu entered the passes he was summoned to serve as Registrar on the Grand Chancellor's staff.

sentences.zh: 時軍旅草創，五禮曠墜。

translations.literal: At that time the army was newly formed and the Five Rites lay in ruin.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the army was newly formed and the Five Rites lay in ruin.

sentences.zh: 威既博物，多識舊儀，朝章國典，皆其所定，禪代文翰多參預焉。

translations.literal: Wei was broadly learned and knew many old protocols; court regulations and state statutes were largely what he fixed, and he took part in many documents of the abdication and succession.
translations.idiomatic: Wei was broadly learned and knew many old protocols; court regulations and state statutes were largely his work, and he took part in many documents of the abdication and succession.

sentences.zh: 高祖常謂裴寂曰：「叔孫通不能加也。」

translations.literal: Gaozu often told Pei Ji, "Shusun Tong could not surpass him."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu often told Pei Ji, "Shusun Tong could not surpass him."

sentences.zh: 武德元年，拜內史令。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wude he was appointed Secretariat Director.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Wude he was appointed Secretariat Director.

sentences.zh: 威奏議雍容，多引古為諭，高祖甚親重之，或引入臥內，常為膝席。

translations.literal: Wei's memorials and deliberations were composed and easy; he often cited antiquity as illustration; Gaozu was very close to and valued him, sometimes bringing him into the sleeping quarters and regularly seating him on the knee-cushion.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's memorials were composed and easy; he often cited antiquity as illustration; Gaozu held him in great affection, sometimes brought him into the sleeping quarters, and regularly seated him on the knee-cushion.

sentences.zh: 又嘗謂曰：「昔周朝有八柱國之貴，吾與公家咸登此職。

translations.literal: He also once said to him, "In antiquity the Zhou had the nobility of the Eight Pillar States; your house and mine both attained this rank.
translations.idiomatic: He also once said to him, "In antiquity the Zhou had the nobility of the Eight Pillar States; your house and mine both attained this rank.

sentences.zh: 今我已為天子，公為內史令，本同末異，乃不平矣。」

translations.literal: Now I am Son of Heaven and you are Secretariat Director—we were alike at the root yet differ at the branch; this is indeed unequal."
translations.idiomatic: Now I am Son of Heaven and you are Secretariat Director—we were alike at the root yet differ at the branch; this is indeed unequal."

sentences.zh: 威謝曰：「臣家昔在漢朝，再為外戚，至於後魏，三處外家，陛下隆興，復出皇后。

translations.literal: Wei thanked him, saying, "My house in the Han was twice imperial affines; under the Later Wei it was thrice an affinal house; Your Majesty's glorious rise has again produced an empress.
translations.idiomatic: Wei thanked him, saying, "My house in the Han was twice imperial affines; under the Later Wei it was thrice an affinal house; Your Majesty's glorious rise has again produced an empress.

sentences.zh: 臣又階緣戚裡，位忝鳳池，自惟叨濫，曉夕兢懼。」

translations.literal: I have again climbed by reason of affinal kinship to a post unworthy of the Phoenix Pool; reflecting on my presumption, morning and evening I tremble with fear."
translations.idiomatic: I have again risen through affinal kinship to a post unworthy of the Phoenix Pool; reflecting on my presumption, morning and evening I tremble with fear."

sentences.zh: 高祖笑曰：「比見關東人與崔、盧為婚，猶自矜伐，公代為帝戚，不亦貴乎！」

translations.literal: Gaozu laughed and said, "I have lately seen men east of the Pass marry with the Cui and Lu clans and still boast of it—are you not nobler, generation after generation an imperial affine?"
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu laughed and said, "I have lately seen men east of the Pass marry with the Cui and Lu clans and still boast of it—are you not nobler, generation after generation an imperial affine?"

sentences.zh: 及寢疾，高祖自往臨問。

translations.literal: When he took to his bed with illness, Gaozu went in person to inquire after him.
translations.idiomatic: When he fell ill, Gaozu went in person to inquire after him.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，家無餘財，遺令薄葬。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died; his household had no surplus wealth, and his final instructions were for a simple burial.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he died; his household had no surplus wealth, and his final instructions were for a simple burial.

sentences.zh: 謚曰靖，贈同州刺史，追封延安郡公。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Tranquil; he was posthumously made Prefect of Tongzhou and enfeoffed as Duke of Yan'an commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title was Tranquil; he was posthumously appointed Prefect of Tongzhou and enfeoffed as Duke of Yan'an.

sentences.zh: 葬日，詔太子及百官並出臨送。

translations.literal: On the day of burial, an edict ordered the crown prince and all officials to go out and attend the send-off.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of burial, an edict ordered the crown prince and all officials to attend the send-off.

sentences.zh: 有文集十捲。

translations.literal: He left collected literary works in ten fascicles.
translations.idiomatic: He left collected literary works in ten fascicles.

sentences.zh: 子惲嗣，官至岐州刺史。

translations.literal: His son Yun succeeded him and rose to Prefect of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yun succeeded him and rose to the post of Prefect of Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 威兄子軌，從兄子抗，並知名。

translations.literal: Wei's nephew Gui and his clansman's son Kang were both well known.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's nephew Gui and his clansman's son Kang were both well known.

sentences.zh: 軌，字士則，周雍州牧、酂國公恭之子也。

translations.literal: Gui, courtesy name Shize, was the son of Zhou's Regional Governor of Yongzhou and Duke of Zan, Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Gui, whose courtesy name was Shize, was the son of Zhou's Regional Governor of Yongzhou and Duke of Zan, Gong.

sentences.zh: 隋大業中，為資陽郡東曹掾，後去官歸於家。

translations.literal: In the Daye era of the Sui he served as Eastern Bureau Attendant of Ziyang commandery, then left office and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daye reign of the Sui he served as Eastern Bureau Attendant of Ziyang commandery, then left office and returned home.

sentences.zh: 義兵起，軌聚眾千餘人，迎謁於長春宮。

translations.literal: When the righteous army rose, Gui gathered more than a thousand men and went to pay respects at Everlasting Spring Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When the uprising began, Gui gathered more than a thousand men and went to pay respects at Everlasting Spring Palace.

sentences.zh: 高祖見之，大悅，降席握手，語及平生，賜良馬十匹，使掠地渭南。

translations.literal: When Gaozu saw him he was greatly pleased, came down from his seat to clasp his hand, spoke of their whole lives, bestowed ten fine horses, and sent him to seize territory south of the Wei.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu saw him he was greatly pleased, came down from his seat to clasp his hand, spoke of their whole lives, bestowed ten fine horses, and sent him to seize territory south of the Wei.

sentences.zh: 軌先下永豐倉，收兵得五千人。

translations.literal: Gui first took Yongfeng Granary and gathered troops to five thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Gui first took Yongfeng Granary and gathered a force of five thousand men.

sentences.zh: 從平京城，封贊皇縣公，拜大丞相諮議參軍。

translations.literal: He followed in the pacification of the capital, was enfeoffed as Duke of Zanhuang county, and appointed Advisory Attendant of the Grand Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the pacification of the capital, was enfeoffed as Duke of Zanhuang county, and appointed Advisory Attendant on the Grand Chancellor's staff.

sentences.zh: 時稽胡賊五萬餘人掠宜春，軌討之。

translations.literal: At that time more than fifty thousand Ji Hu bandits raided Yichun; Gui campaigned against them.
translations.idiomatic: At that time more than fifty thousand Ji Hu bandits raided Yichun; Gui campaigned against them.

sentences.zh: 行次黃欽山，與賊相遇，賊乘高縱火，王師稍卻。

translations.literal: Marching to Huangqin Mountain he met the bandits; the bandits took the high ground and set fires, and the imperial army fell back somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: Marching to Huangqin Mountain he met the bandits; they took the high ground and set fires, and the imperial army fell back somewhat.

sentences.zh: 軌斬其部將十四人，拔隊中小帥以代之。

translations.literal: Gui beheaded fourteen of his subordinate officers and promoted a minor commander in the ranks to replace them.
translations.idiomatic: Gui beheaded fourteen of his subordinate officers and promoted a minor commander in the ranks to replace them.

sentences.zh: 軌自率數百騎殿於軍後，令之曰：「聞鼓聲有不進者，自後斬之。」

translations.literal: Gui himself led several hundred horsemen in the rear guard of the army and ordered them, "Whoever on hearing the drum does not advance will be beheaded from behind."
translations.idiomatic: Gui himself led several hundred horsemen in the rear guard and ordered, "Whoever on hearing the drum does not advance will be beheaded from behind."

sentences.zh: 既聞鼓，士卒爭先赴敵，賊射之，不能止，因大破之，斬首千餘級，虜男女二萬口。

translations.literal: Once the drum was heard, the soldiers vied to rush the enemy; the bandits shot at them but could not stop them; thereby he inflicted a great defeat, beheading more than a thousand, and capturing twenty thousand men and women.
translations.idiomatic: Once the drum sounded, the soldiers vied to rush the enemy; the bandits shot at them but could not stop them; he inflicted a great defeat, beheading more than a thousand, and capturing twenty thousand men and women.

sentences.zh: 武德元年，授太子詹事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wude he was appointed Steward of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Wude he was appointed Steward of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 會赤排羌作亂，與薛舉叛將鐘俱仇同寇漢中。

translations.literal: It happened that the Red-Plank Qiang rebelled, and together with Xue Ju's defector Zhong Juchou they raided Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that the Red-Plank Qiang rebelled, and together with Xue Ju's defector Zhong Juchou they raided Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 拜軌秦州總管，與賊連戰皆捷，餘黨悉降。

translations.literal: Gui was appointed Regional Commander of Qinzhou; in successive battles with the rebels he was victorious, and the remaining factions all submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Gui was appointed Regional Commander of Qinzhou; in successive battles with the rebels he was victorious, and the remaining factions all submitted.

sentences.zh: 進封酂國公。

translations.literal: He was advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of the State of Zan.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced in rank to Duke of Zan.

sentences.zh: 三年，遷益州道行台左僕射，許以便宜從事。

translations.literal: In the third year he was transferred to Left Vice Director of the Yizhou Grand Commission, with permission to act as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was transferred to Left Vice Director of the Yizhou Grand Commission, with permission to act as circumstances required.

sentences.zh: 屬党項寇松州，詔軌援之，又令扶州刺史蔣善合與軌連勢。

translations.literal: It happened that the Tangut raided Songzhou; an edict ordered Gui to reinforce it, and also directed Prefect of Fuzhou Jiang Shanhe to join forces with Gui.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that the Tangut raided Songzhou; an edict ordered Gui to reinforce it, and also directed Prefect of Fuzhou Jiang Shanhe to join forces with him.

sentences.zh: 時党項引吐谷渾之眾，其鋒甚銳。

translations.literal: At that time the Tangut drew the forces of Tuyuhun; their spearhead was very sharp.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Tangut drew the forces of Tuyuhun; their attack was very fierce.

sentences.zh: 軌師未至，善合先期至鉗川，遇賊力戰，走之。

translations.literal: Gui's army had not yet arrived when Shanhe reached Qianchuan ahead of schedule, met the enemy in fierce battle, and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: Gui's army had not yet arrived when Shanhe reached Qianchuan ahead of schedule, met the enemy in fierce battle, and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 軌復軍於臨洮，進擊左封，破其部眾。

translations.literal: Gui regrouped his army at Lintao, advanced to attack Zuofeng, and broke their tribal forces.
translations.idiomatic: Gui regrouped his army at Lintao, advanced to attack Zuofeng, and broke their tribal forces.

sentences.zh: 尋令率所部兵從太宗討王世充於洛陽。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was ordered to lead his troops in following Taizong to campaign against Wang Shichong at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was ordered to lead his troops in following Taizong to campaign against Wang Shichong at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 四年，還益州。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he returned to Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he returned to Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 時蜀土寇往往聚結，悉討平之。

translations.literal: At that time bandits in Shu often gathered; he campaigned against and pacified them all.
translations.idiomatic: At that time bandits in Shu often gathered; he campaigned against and pacified them all.

sentences.zh: 軌每臨戎對寇，或經旬月，身不解甲。

translations.literal: Whenever Gui faced the enemy in battle, sometimes for ten days or a month he would not remove his armor.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Gui faced the enemy in battle, sometimes for ten days or a month he would not remove his armor.

sentences.zh: 其部眾無貴賤少長，不恭命即立斬之。

translations.literal: Among his troops, whether noble or base, young or old, whoever did not respect his orders was immediately beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Among his troops, whether noble or base, young or old, whoever did not obey his orders was immediately beheaded.

sentences.zh: 每日吏士多被鞭撻，流血滿庭，見者莫不重足股慄。

translations.literal: Every day many clerks and soldiers were flogged until blood filled the courtyard; those who saw it all walked with doubled steps and trembling thighs.
translations.idiomatic: Every day many clerks and soldiers were flogged until blood filled the courtyard; those who saw it walked in fear with trembling legs.

sentences.zh: 軌初入蜀，將其甥以為心腹，嘗夜出，呼之不以時至，怒而斬之。

translations.literal: When Gui first entered Shu he took his nephew as a trusted confidant; once at night he went out and called him, but because he did not arrive in time, Gui in anger beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: When Gui first entered Shu he took his nephew as a trusted confidant; once at night he went out and called him, but because he did not arrive in time, Gui in anger beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 每誡家僮不得出外。

translations.literal: He constantly warned his household servants not to go outside.
translations.idiomatic: He constantly warned his household servants not to go outside.

sentences.zh: 嘗遣奴就官廚取漿而悔之，謂奴曰：「我誠使汝，要當斬汝頭以明法耳！」

translations.literal: Once he sent a slave to the official kitchen to fetch broth and then regretted it, saying to the slave, "I truly sent you, but I must behead you to make the law clear!"
translations.idiomatic: Once he sent a slave to the official kitchen to fetch broth and then regretted it, saying to the slave, "I truly sent you, but I must behead you to make the law clear!"

sentences.zh: 遣其部將收奴斬之。

translations.literal: He sent his subordinate officer to seize the slave and behead him.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his subordinate officer to seize the slave and behead him.

sentences.zh: 其奴稱冤，監刑者猶豫未決，軌怒，俱斬之。

translations.literal: The slave cried that he was wronged; the officer overseeing the execution hesitated and did not decide; Gui in anger beheaded them both.
translations.idiomatic: The slave cried that he was wronged; the officer overseeing the execution hesitated; Gui in anger beheaded them both.

sentences.zh: 行台郎中趙弘安，知名士也，軌動輒榜箠，歲至數百。

translations.literal: The Grand Commission Director Zhao Hong'an was a well-known scholar; Gui whenever he moved would have him beaten with the cudgel, reaching several hundred times a year.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Commission Director Zhao Hong'an was a well-known scholar; Gui had him beaten with the cudgel whenever he moved, reaching several hundred times a year.

sentences.zh: 後徵入朝，賜坐御榻，軌容儀不肅，又坐而對詔，高祖大怒，因謂曰：「公之入蜀，車騎、驃騎從者二十人，為公所斬略盡，我隴種車騎，未足給公。」

translations.literal: Later he was summoned to court and granted a seat on the imperial couch; Gui's bearing was not reverent, and he also sat while responding to the edict; Gaozu was greatly angered and therefore said, "When you entered Shu, twenty attendants of chariot and cavalry and swift cavalry followed you, and you have nearly beheaded them all; my Longzhong chariot and cavalry are not enough to supply you."
translations.idiomatic: Later he was summoned to court and granted a seat on the imperial couch; Gui's bearing was not reverent, and he also sat while responding to the edict; Gaozu was greatly angered and said, "When you entered Shu, twenty attendants of chariot and cavalry followed you, and you have nearly beheaded them all; my Longzhong chariot and cavalry are not enough to supply you."

sentences.zh: 詔下獄，俄而釋之，還鎮益州。

translations.literal: An edict sent him to prison; soon afterward he was released and returned to garrison Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: An edict sent him to prison; soon afterward he was released and returned to garrison Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 軌與行台尚書韋雲起、郭行方素不協。

translations.literal: Gui and the Grand Commission Directors Wei Yunqi and Guo Xingfang had long been at odds.
translations.idiomatic: Gui and the Grand Commission Directors Wei Yunqi and Guo Xingfang had long been at odds.

sentences.zh: 及隱太子誅，有詔下益州，軌藏諸懷中，雲起問曰：「詔書安在？」

translations.literal: When the Hidden Crown Prince was executed, an edict was sent down to Yizhou; Gui hid it in his bosom; Yunqi asked, "Where is the edict?"
translations.idiomatic: When the Hidden Crown Prince was executed, an edict was sent down to Yizhou; Gui hid it in his bosom; Yunqi asked, "Where is the edict?"

sentences.zh: 軌不之示，但曰：「卿欲反矣！」

translations.literal: Gui did not show it but only said, "You wish to rebel!"
translations.idiomatic: Gui did not show it but only said, "You wish to rebel!"

sentences.zh: 執而殺之。

translations.literal: He seized and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: He seized and killed him.

sentences.zh: 行方大懼，奔於京師，軌追斬不及。

translations.literal: Xingfang was greatly afraid and fled to the capital; Gui pursued but could not catch and behead him.
translations.idiomatic: Xingfang was greatly afraid and fled to the capital; Gui pursued but could not catch and kill him.

sentences.zh: 是歲，行台廢，即授益州大都督，加食邑六百戶。

translations.literal: That year the Grand Commission was abolished; he was at once appointed Grand Governor of Yizhou and given an additional fief of six hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Grand Commission was abolished; he was at once appointed Grand Governor of Yizhou and given an additional fief of six hundred households.

sentences.zh: 貞觀元年，征授右衛大將軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenguan he was summoned and appointed Grand General of the Right Guards.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhenguan he was summoned and appointed Grand General of the Right Guards.

sentences.zh: 二年，出為洛州都督。

translations.literal: In the second year he was sent out as Regional Commander of Luozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was sent out as Regional Commander of Luozhou.

sentences.zh: 洛陽因隋末喪亂，人多浮偽。

translations.literal: Because of the disorders at the end of the Sui, the people of Luoyang were largely shiftless and false.
translations.idiomatic: Because of the disorders at the end of the Sui, the people of Luoyang were largely shiftless and deceitful.

sentences.zh: 軌並遣務農，各令屬縣有游手怠惰者皆按之。

translations.literal: Gui together dispatched agricultural commissioners and ordered each subordinate county to investigate all idlers and the lazy.
translations.idiomatic: Gui dispatched agricultural commissioners and ordered each subordinate county to investigate all idlers and the lazy.

sentences.zh: 由是人吏懾憚，風化整肅。

translations.literal: Thereby officials and clerks were awed and fearful, and customs were put in order and made strict.
translations.idiomatic: Thereby officials and clerks were awed into obedience, and local customs were brought into strict order.

sentences.zh: 四年，卒官，贈并州都督。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he died in office and was posthumously made Regional Commander of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he died in office and was posthumously appointed Regional Commander of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 子奉節嗣，尚高祖永嘉公主，歷左衛將軍、秦州都督。

translations.literal: His son Fengjie succeeded him, married Gaozu's daughter Princess Yongjia, and served in succession as General of the Left Guards and Regional Commander of Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fengjie succeeded him, married Gaozu's daughter Princess Yongjia, and rose through the posts of General of the Left Guards and Regional Commander of Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 軌弟琮，亦有武干，隋左親衛。

translations.literal: Gui's younger brother Cong also had martial talent and served the Sui as Left Palace Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Gui's younger brother Cong also had martial talent and served the Sui as Left Palace Guard.

sentences.zh: 大業末，犯法，亡命奔太原，依於高祖。

translations.literal: At the end of Daye he violated the law, fled for his life to Taiyuan, and attached himself to Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Daye he broke the law, fled for his life to Taiyuan, and attached himself to Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 琮與太宗有宿憾，每自疑。

translations.literal: Cong and Taizong had an old grievance, and he constantly suspected himself.
translations.idiomatic: Cong and Taizong had an old grievance, and he constantly suspected himself.

sentences.zh: 太宗方蒐羅英傑，降禮納之，出入臥內，其意乃解。

translations.literal: Taizong was then gathering outstanding men, lowered ritual to receive him, and had him enter and leave the sleeping quarters; only then did his mind ease.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong was then gathering outstanding men, received him with lowered ceremony, and had him enter and leave the sleeping quarters; only then did his mind ease.

sentences.zh: 及將義舉，琮協贊大謀。

translations.literal: When the righteous uprising was about to be raised, Cong assisted and supported the great plan.
translations.idiomatic: When the uprising was about to be raised, Cong assisted and supported the great plan.

sentences.zh: 大將軍府建，為統軍。

translations.literal: When the Grand General's headquarters was established, he was made Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: When the Grand General's headquarters was established, he was made Commander-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 從平西河，破霍邑，拜金紫光祿大夫、扶風郡公。

translations.literal: He followed in the pacification of Xihe and the defeat at Huoyi, and was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon and Duke of Fufeng commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the pacification of Xihe and the victory at Huoyi, and was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon and Duke of Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 尋從劉文靜擊屈突通於潼關，通遣裨將桑顯和來逼文靜，義軍不利。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he followed Liu Wenjing in attacking Qu Tutong at Tong Pass; Tutong sent his deputy general Sang Xianhe to press Wenjing, and the righteous army fared ill.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he followed Liu Wenjing in attacking Qu Tutong at Tong Pass; Tutong sent his deputy general Sang Xianhe to press Wenjing, and the rebel army fared ill.

sentences.zh: 琮與段志玄等力戰久之，隋軍大潰，通遁走。

translations.literal: Cong together with Duan Zhixuan and others fought fiercely for a long time; the Sui army was greatly routed and Tutong fled.
translations.idiomatic: Cong together with Duan Zhixuan and others fought fiercely for a long time; the Sui army was routed and Tutong fled.

sentences.zh: 琮率輕騎追至稠桑，獲通而返。

translations.literal: Cong led light cavalry in pursuit to Chousang, captured Tutong, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Cong led light cavalry in pursuit to Chousang, captured Tutong, and returned.

sentences.zh: 進兵東略，下陝縣，拔太原倉。

translations.literal: He advanced eastward in campaign, took Shaan county, and seized Taiyuan Granary.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced eastward in campaign, took Shaan county, and seized Taiyuan Granary.

sentences.zh: 拜右領軍大將軍，賜物五百段。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grand General of the Right Guards and bestowed five hundred bolts of goods.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Grand General of the Right Guards and bestowed five hundred bolts of goods.

sentences.zh: 時隋河陽都尉獨孤武潛謀歸國，乃令琮以步騎一萬自柏崖道應接之。

translations.literal: At that time the Sui Commandant of Heyang, Dugu Wu, secretly plotted to submit to the new state; Cong was ordered to take ten thousand foot and horse by the Baiya route to meet and support him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Sui Commandant of Heyang, Dugu Wu, secretly plotted to submit to the Tang cause; Cong was ordered to take ten thousand foot and horse by the Baiya route to meet and support him.

sentences.zh: 遲留不進，武見殺，坐是除名。

translations.literal: He delayed and did not advance; Wu was killed, and for this Cong was removed from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: He delayed and did not advance; Wu was killed, and for this Cong was struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 武德初，以元謀勳特恕一死，拜右屯衛大將軍，復轉右領軍大將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wude, because of his merit in the founding plot he was specially pardoned from death, appointed Grand General of the Right Garrison Guards, and again transferred to Grand General of the Right Guards.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Wude, because of his merit in the founding plot he was specially pardoned from death, appointed Grand General of the Right Garrison Guards, and again transferred to Grand General of the Right Guards.

sentences.zh: 時將圖洛陽，遣琮留守陝城，以督糧運。

translations.literal: At that time they were planning Luoyang; Cong was sent to garrison Shaan city and supervise grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: At that time they were planning the campaign for Luoyang; Cong was sent to garrison Shaan city and supervise grain transport.

sentences.zh: 王世充遣其驍將羅士信來斷糧道，琮潛使人說以利害，士信遂帥眾降。

translations.literal: Wang Shichong sent his fierce general Luo Shixin to cut the grain route; Cong secretly sent men to persuade him of gain and loss, and Shixin thereupon led his followers in submission.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shichong sent his fierce general Luo Shixin to cut the grain route; Cong secretly sent men to persuade him of gain and loss, and Shixin thereupon led his followers in submission.

sentences.zh: 及從平東都，賞物一千四百段。

translations.literal: When he followed in the pacification of the Eastern Capital, he was rewarded with fourteen hundred bolts of goods.
translations.idiomatic: When he took part in the pacification of the Eastern Capital, he was rewarded with fourteen hundred bolts of goods.

sentences.zh: 後以本官檢校晉州總管。

translations.literal: Later, in his former office, he was made acting Regional Commander of Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made acting Regional Commander of Jinzhou in his former rank.

sentences.zh: 尋從隱太子討平劉黑闥，以功封譙國公，賞黃金五十斤。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he followed the Hidden Crown Prince in pacifying Liu Heita; for his merit he was enfeoffed as Duke of the State of Qiao and rewarded with fifty jin of gold.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he followed the Hidden Crown Prince in pacifying Liu Heita; for his merit he was enfeoffed as Duke of Qiao and rewarded with fifty jin of gold.

sentences.zh: 未幾而卒。

translations.literal: Before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died.

sentences.zh: 高祖以佐命之舊，甚悼之，贈左衛大將軍，謚曰敬。

translations.literal: Gaozu, because of his old merit in assisting the mandate, grieved deeply for him, posthumously made him Grand General of the Left Guards, and gave the posthumous title Respectful.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu, because of his old merit in assisting the mandate, grieved deeply for him, posthumously appointed him Grand General of the Left Guards, and gave the posthumous title Respectful.

sentences.zh: 永徽五年，重贈特進。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yonghui he was again posthumously made Special Advancement.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Yonghui he was again posthumously appointed Special Advancement.

sentences.zh: 抗，字道生，太穆皇后之從兄也，隋洛州總管、陳國公榮之子也。

translations.literal: Kang, courtesy name Daosheng, was a cousin on his father's side to Empress Taimu and the son of the Sui Regional Commander of Luozhou and Duke of the State of Chen, Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Kang, whose courtesy name was Daosheng, was a paternal cousin of Empress Taimu and the son of the Sui Regional Commander of Luozhou and Duke of Chen, Rong.

sentences.zh: 母，隋文帝萬安公主。

translations.literal: His mother was Emperor Wen of the Sui's Princess Wan'an.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was Emperor Wen of the Sui's Princess Wan'an.

sentences.zh: 抗在隋以帝甥甚見崇寵。

translations.literal: Kang under the Sui, as the emperor's nephew-by-marriage, was greatly honored and favored.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Sui, as the emperor's nephew-by-marriage, Kang was greatly honored and favored.

sentences.zh: 少入太學，略涉書史，釋褐千牛備身、儀同三司。

translations.literal: In youth he entered the Imperial Academy, ranged briefly through books and histories, and on leaving the sackcloth was made Palace Guard Attendant and Companions of the Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he entered the Imperial Academy, read briefly in books and histories, and on entering service was made Palace Guard Attendant and Companion of the Third Rank.

sentences.zh: 屬其父寢疾，抗躬親扶侍，衣不解帶者五十餘日。

translations.literal: When his father took to his bed with illness, Kang personally attended and supported him, not removing his belt for more than fifty days.
translations.idiomatic: When his father fell ill, Kang personally attended him and did not remove his belt for more than fifty days.

sentences.zh: 及居喪，哀毀過禮。

translations.literal: When he entered mourning, his grief and devastation exceeded the rites.
translations.idiomatic: In mourning his grief exceeded the rites.

sentences.zh: 後襲爵陳國公，累轉梁州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he inherited the enfeoffment as Duke of the State of Chen and was promoted in succession to Prefect of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later he inherited the title Duke of Chen and rose through successive posts to Prefect of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 將之官，隋文帝幸其第，命抗及公主酣宴，如家人之禮，賞賜極厚。

translations.literal: When he was about to take up his post, Emperor Wen of the Sui visited his residence, ordered Kang and the princess to feast deeply, treated them with the ritual of family members, and bestowed extremely rich rewards.
translations.idiomatic: When he was about to take up his post, Emperor Wen visited his residence, ordered Kang and the princess to feast deeply, treated them with family ritual, and bestowed extremely rich rewards.

sentences.zh: 母卒，號慟絕而復甦者數焉，文帝令宮人至第，節其哭泣。

translations.literal: When his mother died he wailed until he fainted and revived several times; Emperor Wen sent palace women to his residence to moderate his weeping.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he wailed until he fainted and revived several times; Emperor Wen sent palace women to his residence to moderate his weeping.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，起為岐州刺史，轉幽州總管，政並以寬惠聞。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was recalled to serve as Prefect of Qizhou, then transferred to Regional Commander of Youzhou; his government in both posts was known for leniency and kindness.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he was recalled to serve as Prefect of Qizhou, then transferred to Regional Commander of Youzhou; his government in both posts was known for leniency and kindness.

sentences.zh: 及漢王諒作亂，煬帝恐其為變，遣李子雄馳往代之。

translations.literal: When Prince of Han Liang rebelled, Emperor Yang feared Kang might change sides and sent Li Zixiong posthaste to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Han Liang rebelled, Emperor Yang feared Kang might change sides and sent Li Zixiong posthaste to replace him.

sentences.zh: 子雄因言抗得諒書而不奏，按之無驗，以疑貳除名。

translations.literal: Zixiong reported that Kang had received Liang's letter but did not memorialize it; investigation found no proof, but on suspicion of divided loyalty he was removed from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Zixiong reported that Kang had received Liang's letter but did not memorialize it; investigation found no proof, but on suspicion of divided loyalty he was struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 抗與高祖少相親狎，及楊玄感作亂，高祖統兵隴右，抗言於高祖曰：「玄感抑為發蹤耳！

translations.literal: Kang and Gaozu had been close and familiar in youth; when Yang Xuangan rebelled and Gaozu commanded troops in Longyou, Kang said to Gaozu, "Xuangan is only the one who sets the hounds running!
translations.idiomatic: Kang and Gaozu had been close in youth; when Yang Xuangan rebelled and Gaozu commanded troops in Longyou, Kang said to Gaozu, "Xuangan is only the one who sets the hounds running!

sentences.zh: 李氏有名圖籙，可乘其便，天之所啟也。」

translations.literal: The Li house has a famous chart and register—one may seize this opportunity; it is what Heaven has opened."
translations.idiomatic: The Li house has a famous chart and register—one may seize this opportunity; it is what Heaven has opened."

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「無為禍始，何言之妄也！」

translations.literal: Gaozu said, "Do not be the beginning of disaster—how wild your words!"
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said, "Do not be the beginning of disaster—how wild your words!"

sentences.zh: 大業末，抗於靈武巡長城以伺盜賊，及聞高祖定京城，抗對眾而忭曰：「此吾家妹婿也，豁達有大度，真撥亂之主矣！」

translations.literal: Near the end of Daye, Kang at Lingwu patrolled the Long Wall to watch for bandits; when he heard Gaozu had secured the capital, Kang said to the assembled men in delight, "This is my family's son-in-law—open and magnanimous, truly a lord who can put chaos in order!"
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Daye, Kang at Lingwu patrolled the Long Wall to watch for bandits; when he heard Gaozu had secured the capital, Kang said to the assembled men in delight, "This is my family's son-in-law—open and magnanimous, truly a lord who can put chaos in order!"

sentences.zh: 因歸長安。

translations.literal: Thereupon he returned to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he returned to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 高祖見之大悅，握手引坐曰：「李氏竟能成事，何如？」

translations.literal: When Gaozu saw him he was greatly pleased, clasped his hand and drew him to sit, saying, "The Li house has actually been able to accomplish the enterprise—what do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu saw him he was greatly pleased, clasped his hand and drew him to sit, saying, "The Li house has actually accomplished the enterprise—what do you think?"

sentences.zh: 因縱酒為樂。

translations.literal: Thereupon they drank freely for pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon they drank freely for pleasure.

sentences.zh: 尋拜將作大匠。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed Master of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was appointed Master of Works.

sentences.zh: 武德元年，以本官兼納言。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wude he was made concurrent Remonstrator in his former office.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Wude he was made concurrent Remonstrator in his former office.

sentences.zh: 高祖聽朝，或升御坐，退朝之後，延入臥內，命之舍敬，縱酒談謔，敦平生之款。

translations.literal: When Gaozu held court, Kang sometimes ascended the imperial seat; after court was dismissed he was invited into the sleeping quarters, ordered to set aside reverence, and they drank freely, jested, and renewed the warmth of their lifelong friendship.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu held court, Kang sometimes ascended the imperial seat; after court was dismissed he was invited into the sleeping quarters, told to set aside ceremony, and they drank freely, jested, and renewed their lifelong friendship.

sentences.zh: 常侍宴移時，或留宿禁內。
