translations.literal: He constantly attended feasts for long stretches, or stayed overnight within the forbidden precincts.
translations.idiomatic: He constantly attended feasts for long stretches, or stayed overnight within the forbidden precincts.

sentences.zh: 高祖每呼為兄而不名也，宮內咸稱為舅。

translations.literal: Gaozu always called him elder brother without using his name; within the palace all called him maternal uncle.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu always called him elder brother without using his name; within the palace all called him maternal uncle.

sentences.zh: 常陪侍游宴，不知朝務。

translations.literal: He constantly accompanied him in excursions and feasts and knew nothing of court affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He constantly accompanied him in excursions and feasts and knew nothing of court affairs.

sentences.zh: 轉左武候大將軍，領左右千牛備身大將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Grand General of the Left Martial Guards and concurrently Grand General of the Left and Right Palace Guard Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Grand General of the Left Martial Guards and concurrently Grand General of the Left and Right Palace Guard Attendants.

sentences.zh: 尋從太宗平薛舉，勳居第一。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he followed Taizong in pacifying Xue Ju; his merit ranked first.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he followed Taizong in pacifying Xue Ju; his merit ranked first.

sentences.zh: 四年，又從征王世充。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he again followed in the campaign against Wang Shichong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he again followed in the campaign against Wang Shichong.

sentences.zh: 及東都平，冊勳太廟者九人，抗與從弟軌俱預焉。

translations.literal: When the Eastern Capital was pacified, nine men had their merit recorded in the Imperial Ancestral Temple; Kang and his clansman Gui were both among them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Eastern Capital was pacified, nine men had their merit recorded in the Imperial Ancestral Temple; Kang and his clansman Gui were both among them.

sentences.zh: 朝廷榮之，賜女樂一部、金寶萬計。

translations.literal: The court honored them and bestowed a set of female musicians and treasures numbering in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: The court honored them and bestowed a set of female musicians and treasures numbering in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 武德四年，因侍宴暴卒，贈司空，謚曰密。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Wude he suddenly died while attending a feast; he was posthumously made Minister of Works and given the posthumous title Secret.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Wude he suddenly died while attending a feast; he was posthumously appointed Minister of Works and given the posthumous title Secret.

sentences.zh: 子衍。

translations.literal: His son Yan.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Yan.

sentences.zh: 衍嗣，官至左武衛將軍。

translations.literal: Yan succeeded him and rose to General of the Left Martial Guards.
translations.idiomatic: Yan succeeded him and rose to the post of General of the Left Martial Guards.

sentences.zh: 時抗群從內三品七人，四品、五品十餘人，尚主三人，妃數人，冠冕之盛，當朝無比。

translations.literal: At that time among Kang's clansmen there were seven of the third rank within the palace, more than ten of the fourth and fifth ranks, three who married princesses, and several who became imperial consorts; the splendor of caps and coronets was unmatched in the court.
translations.idiomatic: At that time among Kang's clansmen there were seven of the third rank within the palace, more than ten of the fourth and fifth ranks, three who married princesses, and several who became imperial consorts; the splendor of their ranks was unmatched at court.

sentences.zh: 靜，字元休，抗第二子也。

translations.literal: Jing, courtesy name Yuanxiu, was Kang's second son.
translations.idiomatic: Jing, whose courtesy name was Yuanxiu, was Kang's second son.

sentences.zh: 武德初，累轉并州大總管府長史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wude he was promoted in succession to Chief Clerk of the Bingzhou Grand Governor's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Wude he rose through successive posts to Chief Clerk of the Bingzhou Grand Governor's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 時突厥數為邊患，師旅歲興，軍糧不屬，靜表請太原置屯田以省饋運。

translations.literal: At that time the Turks repeatedly became a frontier peril; armies were raised year after year and military grain was not continuous; Jing memorialized requesting that garrison fields be established at Taiyuan to economize on transport of provisions.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Turks repeatedly raided the frontier; armies were raised year after year and military grain ran short; Jing memorialized requesting garrison fields at Taiyuan to economize on transport of provisions.

sentences.zh: 時議者以民物凋零，不宜動眾，書奏不省。

translations.literal: At that time debaters held that the people and goods were withered and it was not fitting to mobilize the masses; the memorial was not examined.
translations.idiomatic: At that time debaters held that the people and goods were depleted and it was not fitting to mobilize the masses; the memorial went unanswered.

sentences.zh: 靜頻上書，辭甚切至。

translations.literal: Jing repeatedly submitted memorials, his words very urgent and direct.
translations.idiomatic: Jing repeatedly submitted memorials, his words very urgent and direct.

sentences.zh: 於是征靜入朝，與裴寂、蕭瑀、封德彝等爭論於殿庭，寂等不能屈，竟從靜議。

translations.literal: Thereupon Jing was summoned to court and debated in the hall with Pei Ji, Xiao Yu, Feng Deyi, and others; Ji and the rest could not overcome him, and in the end Jing's proposal was followed.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Jing was summoned to court and debated in the hall with Pei Ji, Xiao Yu, Feng Deyi, and others; Ji and the rest could not overcome him, and in the end his proposal was followed.

sentences.zh: 歲收數千斛，高祖善之，令檢校并州大總管。

translations.literal: Each year several thousand hu were harvested; Gaozu approved this and ordered him to act as inspector of the Bingzhou Grand Governor.
translations.idiomatic: Each year several thousand hu were harvested; Gaozu approved this and ordered him to act as inspector of the Bingzhou Grand Governor.

sentences.zh: 靜又以突厥頻來入寇，請斷石嶺以為障塞，復從之。

translations.literal: Jing also, because the Turks repeatedly came in to raid, requested that Shiling Pass be cut off to serve as a barrier; this too was followed.
translations.idiomatic: Jing also, because the Turks repeatedly raided the borders, requested that Shiling Pass be cut off to serve as a barrier; this too was followed.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，征拜司農卿，封信都男，尋轉夏州都督。

translations.literal: When Taizong took the throne, Jing was summoned and appointed Director of the Directorate of Agriculture, enfeoffed as Baron of Xindu, and soon transferred to Regional Commander of Xiazhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong took the throne, Jing was summoned and appointed Director of the Directorate of Agriculture, enfeoffed as Baron of Xindu, and soon transferred to Regional Commander of Xiazhou.

sentences.zh: 值突厥攜貳，諸將出征，多詣其所。

translations.literal: It happened that the Turks were divided in loyalty; when the generals went out on campaign, many came to his headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that the Turks were divided in loyalty; when the generals went out on campaign, many came to his headquarters.

sentences.zh: 靜知虜中虛實，潛令人間其部落，郁射設所部郁孤尼等九俟斤並率眾歸款，太宗稱善，賜馬百匹、羊千口。

translations.literal: Jing knew the real strength and weakness among the barbarians and secretly sent men to sow division among their tribes; the nine irkin including Yuguni under Yushe's command all led their followers in submission; Taizong praised this and bestowed a hundred horses and a thousand sheep.
translations.idiomatic: Jing knew the real strength and weakness among the barbarians and secretly sent men to sow division among their tribes; the nine irkin including Yuguni under Yushe's command all led their followers in submission; Taizong praised this and bestowed a hundred horses and a thousand sheep.

sentences.zh: 及擒頡利，處其部眾於河南，以為不便，上封曰：「臣聞夷狄者，同夫禽獸，窮則搏噬，群則聚塵。

translations.literal: When Jiali was captured and his tribal followers were settled south of the Yellow River, Jing held this inconvenient and submitted a sealed memorial, saying, "Your servant has heard that the Yi and Di are like birds and beasts: when cornered they strike and devour, when gathered they raise dust.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiali was captured and his tribal followers were settled south of the Yellow River, Jing held this inconvenient and submitted a sealed memorial, saying, "Your servant has heard that the barbarians are like birds and beasts: when cornered they strike and devour, when gathered they raise dust.

sentences.zh: 不可以刑法威，不可以仁義教。

translations.literal: They cannot be awed by penal law, nor instructed by benevolence and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: They cannot be awed by penal law, nor instructed by benevolence and righteousness.

sentences.zh: 衣食仰給，不務耕桑，徒損有為之民，以資無知之虜，得之則無益於治，失之則無損於化。

translations.literal: Their food and clothing depend on others' supply; they do not devote themselves to farming and sericulture; they only harm productive people to support ignorant barbarians—gaining them brings no benefit to government, losing them brings no harm to transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Their food and clothing depend on others' supply; they do not farm or raise silkworms; they only harm productive people to support ignorant barbarians—gaining them brings no benefit to government, losing them brings no harm to order.

sentences.zh: 然彼首丘之情，未易忘也，誠恐一旦變生，犯我王略，愚臣之所深慮。

translations.literal: Yet their feeling for the mound of their birth is not easily forgotten; I truly fear that if change arises in a single day they will violate our royal domain—this is what your foolish servant deeply considers.
translations.idiomatic: Yet their longing for home is not easily forgotten; I truly fear that if change arises in a single day they will violate our royal domain—this is what your foolish servant deeply fears.

sentences.zh: 如臣計者，莫如因其破亡之後，加其無妄之福，假以賢王之號，妻以宗室之女，分其土地，析其部落，使其權弱勢分，易為羈制。

translations.literal: As your servant calculates, nothing is better than after their defeat and ruin to add undeserved blessings, lend them the title of worthy king, marry them to daughters of the imperial clan, divide their lands, and split their tribes so that their power is weak and their force divided and easy to restrain.
translations.idiomatic: As your servant calculates, nothing is better than after their defeat and ruin to add undeserved blessings, lend them the title of worthy king, marry them to daughters of the imperial clan, divide their lands, and split their tribes so that their power is weak and their force divided and easy to restrain.

sentences.zh: 自可永保邊塞，俾為籓臣，此實長轡遠馭之道。」

translations.literal: Thereby the frontier may be forever secured and they made vassal ministers—this is truly the way of long reins and distant driving."
translations.idiomatic: Thereby the frontier may be forever secured and they made vassal ministers—this is truly the way of governing from afar with loose reins."

sentences.zh: 於時務在懷輯，雖未從之，太宗深嘉其志。

translations.literal: At that time the task lay in cherishing and gathering them in; though his plan was not followed, Taizong deeply praised his intent.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the task lay in cherishing and gathering them in; though his plan was not followed, Taizong deeply praised his intent.

sentences.zh: 制曰：「北方之務，悉以相委，以卿為寧朔大使，撫鎮華戎，朕無北顧之憂矣。」

translations.literal: An edict said, "Northern affairs are all entrusted to you; with you as Pacifier of the North Ambassador, comforting and garrisoning Chinese and barbarians, I have no worry of looking north."
translations.idiomatic: An edict said, "Northern affairs are all entrusted to you; with you as Pacifier of the North Ambassador, comforting and garrisoning Chinese and barbarians, I have no worry of looking north."

sentences.zh: 再遷民部尚書。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Minister of the Household.
translations.idiomatic: He was again transferred to Minister of the Household.

sentences.zh: 貞觀九年卒，謚曰肅。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Zhenguan he died; his posthumous title was Solemn.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Zhenguan he died; his posthumous title was Solemn.

sentences.zh: 子逵。

translations.literal: His son Kui.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Kui.

sentences.zh: 逵尚太宗女遂安公主，襲爵信都男。

translations.literal: Kui married Taizong's daughter Princess Suian and inherited the barony of Xindu.
translations.idiomatic: Kui married Taizong's daughter Princess Suian and inherited the barony of Xindu.

sentences.zh: 誕，抗第三子也。

translations.literal: Dan was Kang's third son.
translations.idiomatic: Dan was Kang's third son.

sentences.zh: 隋仁壽中，起家為朝請郎。

translations.literal: In the Renshou era of the Sui he first entered service as Court Requester.
translations.idiomatic: During the Renshou era of the Sui he first entered service as Court Requester.

sentences.zh: 義寧初，辟丞相府祭酒，轉殿中監，封安豐郡公，尚高祖女襄陽公主。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yining he was summoned as Libationer of the Chancellor's headquarters, transferred to Director of the Palace Directorate, enfeoffed as Duke of Anfeng commandery, and married Gaozu's daughter Princess Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yining he was summoned as Libationer on the Chancellor's staff, transferred to Director of the Palace Directorate, enfeoffed as Duke of Anfeng, and married Gaozu's daughter Princess Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 從太宗征薛舉，為元帥府司馬。

translations.literal: He followed Taizong in campaigning against Xue Ju and served as marshal of the Commander's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Taizong in campaigning against Xue Ju and served as marshal on the commander's staff.

sentences.zh: 遷刑部尚書，轉太常卿。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Justice, then to Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Minister of Justice, then to Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 高祖諸少子荊王元景等未出宮者十餘王，所有國司家產之事，皆令誕主之。

translations.literal: More than ten of Gaozu's younger sons, such as Prince of Jing Yuanjing, who had not yet left the palace—all matters of state offices and household property were put under Dan's charge.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten of Gaozu's younger sons, such as Prince of Jing Yuanjing, who had not yet left the palace—all matters of state offices and household property were put under Dan's charge.

sentences.zh: 出為梁州都督。

translations.literal: He was sent out as Regional Commander of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Regional Commander of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，召拜右領軍大將軍，轉大理卿、莘國公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan he was summoned and appointed Grand General of the Right Guards, then transferred to Director of the Court of Judicial Review and Duke of the State of Shen.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Zhenguan he was summoned and appointed Grand General of the Right Guards, then transferred to Director of the Court of Judicial Review and Duke of Shen.

sentences.zh: 修營太廟，賜物五百段。

translations.literal: He oversaw the repair and construction of the Imperial Ancestral Temple and was bestowed five hundred bolts of goods.
translations.idiomatic: He oversaw the repair and construction of the Imperial Ancestral Temple and was bestowed five hundred bolts of goods.

sentences.zh: 復為殿中監，以疾解官，復拜宗正卿。

translations.literal: He again served as Director of the Palace Directorate, then left office because of illness, and was again appointed Director of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: He again served as Director of the Palace Directorate, then left office because of illness, and was again appointed Director of the Imperial Clan.

sentences.zh: 太宗常與之言，昏忘不能對，乃手詔曰：「朕聞為官擇人者治，為人擇官者亂。

translations.literal: Taizong often spoke with him, but he was muddled and forgetful and could not respond; Taizong therefore wrote a personal edict, saying, "Your servant has heard that he who chooses men for offices governs well, and he who chooses offices for men brings disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong often spoke with him, but he was muddled and forgetful and could not respond; Taizong therefore wrote a personal edict, saying, "I have heard that he who chooses men for offices governs well, and he who chooses offices for men brings disorder.

sentences.zh: 竇誕比來精神衰耗，殊異常時。

translations.literal: Dou Dan of late has had his spirit decay and waste, greatly unlike ordinary times.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Dan of late has had his spirit decay and waste, greatly unlike ordinary times.

sentences.zh: 知不肖而任之，睹尸祿而不退，非唯傷風亂政，亦恐為君不明。

translations.literal: Knowing him unworthy yet appointing him, seeing him hold salary without work yet not withdrawing—this not only harms custom and disorders government, but also makes one fear the ruler is not clear-sighted.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing him unworthy yet appointing him, seeing him hold salary without work yet not withdrawing—this not only harms custom and disorders government, but also suggests the ruler is not clear-sighted.

sentences.zh: 考績黜陟，古今常典，誕可光祿大夫還第。」

translations.literal: Examining merit for demotion and promotion is the constant canon of antiquity and today; Dan may return home as Grand Master for Splendid Happiness."
translations.idiomatic: Examining merit for demotion and promotion is the constant canon of antiquity and today; Dan may return home as Grand Master for Splendid Happiness."

sentences.zh: 尋卒，贈工部尚書、荊州刺史，謚曰安。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died; he was posthumously made Minister of Works and Prefect of Jingzhou, with the posthumous title Tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he died; he was posthumously appointed Minister of Works and Prefect of Jingzhou, with the posthumous title Tranquil.

sentences.zh: 子孝慈。

translations.literal: His son Xiaoci.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Xiaoci.

sentences.zh: 孝慈嗣，官至左衛將軍。

translations.literal: Xiaoci succeeded him and rose to General of the Left Guards.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoci succeeded him and rose to the post of General of the Left Guards.

sentences.zh: 孝慈子希玠。

translations.literal: Xiaoci's son Xijue.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoci's son was Xijue.

sentences.zh: 希玠少襲爵，中宗時為禮部尚書，以恩澤賜實封二百五十戶。

translations.literal: Xijue in youth inherited the enfeoffment; in the time of Emperor Zhongzong he was Minister of Rites and by grace was granted a substantive fief of two hundred fifty households.
translations.idiomatic: Xijue inherited the title in youth; under Emperor Zhongzong he served as Minister of Rites and by imperial grace received a substantive fief of two hundred fifty households.

sentences.zh: 開元初為太子少傅、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan he was made Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent and Palace Attendant with the Honored Title of Companions of the Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Kaiyuan he was made Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent and Palace Attendant with Honored Title equal to Companions of the Third Rank.

sentences.zh: 誕少子孝諶，在《外戚傳》。

translations.literal: Dan's younger son Xiaochen is treated in the 《Biography of Imperial Affines》.
translations.idiomatic: Dan's younger son Xiaochen is treated in the 《Biography of Imperial Affines》.

sentences.zh: 竇氏自武德至今，再為外戚，一品三人，三品已上三十餘人，尚主者八人，女為王妃六人，唐世貴盛，莫與為比。

translations.literal: From Wude to the present the Dou clan has twice been imperial affines; three men of the first rank, more than thirty of the third rank and above, eight who married princesses, and six daughters who became imperial princesses-by-marriage—in the Tang age their nobility and splendor had no equal.
translations.idiomatic: From Wude to the present the Dou clan had twice been imperial affines: three men of the first rank, more than thirty of the third rank and above, eight who married princesses, and six daughters who became imperial princesses-by-marriage. In the Tang age their nobility and splendor had no equal.

sentences.zh: 璡，字之推，抗季弟也。

translations.literal: Jin, courtesy name Zhitui, was Kang's youngest younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Jin, whose courtesy name was Zhitui, was Kang's youngest younger brother.

sentences.zh: 大業末，為扶風太守。

translations.literal: At the end of Daye he was Governor of Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Daye he served as Governor of Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 高祖定京師，以郡歸國，歷禮部、民部二尚書。

translations.literal: When Gaozu secured the capital, Jin submitted the commandery to the new state and served in succession as Minister of Rites and Minister of the Household.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu secured the capital, Jin surrendered the commandery and rose through the posts of Minister of Rites and Minister of the Household.

sentences.zh: 從太宗平薛仁杲。

translations.literal: He followed Taizong in pacifying Xue Rengao.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Taizong in pacifying Xue Rengao.

sentences.zh: 尋鎮益州，時蜀中尚多寇賊，璡屢討平之。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he garrisoned Yizhou; at that time Shu still had many bandits and raiders, and Jin repeatedly campaigned and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was posted to Yizhou; bandits still plagued Shu, and Jin repeatedly campaigned and pacified them.

sentences.zh: 時皇甫無逸在蜀，與之不協，璡屢請入朝。

translations.literal: At that time Huangfu Wuyi was in Shu and was not in harmony with him; Jin repeatedly requested to enter court.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Huangfu Wuyi was in Shu and clashed with him; Jin repeatedly asked to return to court.

sentences.zh: 高祖征之，中路詔令還鎮。

translations.literal: Gaozu summoned him, but midway an edict ordered him to return to his garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu summoned him, but midway an edict ordered him back to his post.

sentences.zh: 璡不得志，遂於路左題山，以申鬱積。

translations.literal: Jin did not achieve his wish and thereupon inscribed a mountain by the roadside to express his pent-up feelings.
translations.idiomatic: Frustrated in his ambitions, Jin inscribed a mountain by the roadside to vent his pent-up feelings.

sentences.zh: 有使者至其所，璡宴之臥內，遺以綾綺。

translations.literal: When an envoy came to his place, Jin feasted him in the sleeping quarters and gave him silks and brocades.
translations.idiomatic: When an envoy came to his headquarters, Jin feasted him in his private quarters and gave him silks and brocades.

sentences.zh: 無逸奏其事，坐免官。

translations.literal: Wuyi memorialized the matter, and for this Jin was removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Wuyi memorialized the matter, and Jin was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 未幾，拜秘書監，封鄧國公。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Director of the Secretariat and enfeoffed as Duke of the State of Deng.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed Director of the Secretariat and enfeoffed as Duke of Deng.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，授太子詹事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan he was appointed Steward of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Zhenguan he was made Steward of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 後為將作大匠，修葺洛陽宮。

translations.literal: Later he was made Master of Works and repaired and renovated Luoyang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made Master of Works and oversaw repairs to Luoyang Palace.

sentences.zh: 璡於宮中鑿池起山，崇飾雕麗，虛費功力，太宗怒，遽令毀之。

translations.literal: Jin within the palace dug pools and raised mountains, adorned them with lavish carved ornament, and wasted labor in vain; Taizong was angry and immediately ordered them destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Within the palace Jin dug pools and raised artificial mountains, adorned them with lavish carved ornament, and wasted labor in vain; Taizong was furious and immediately ordered them torn down.

sentences.zh: 坐事免。

translations.literal: For an offense he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed for the offense.

sentences.zh: 會納其女為酆王妃，俄而復位，加右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: It happened that his daughter was taken in marriage as Princess of Feng; soon afterward he was restored to office and made Right Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: When his daughter was taken in marriage as Princess of Feng, he was soon restored to office and made Right Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 七年卒，贈禮部尚書，謚曰安。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he died; he was posthumously made Minister of Rites and given the posthumous title Tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he died; he was posthumously appointed Minister of Rites and given the posthumous title Tranquil.

sentences.zh: 璡頗曉音律，武德中，與太常少卿祖孝孫受詔定正聲雅樂，璡討論故實，撰《正聲調》一卷，行於代。

translations.literal: Jin was quite versed in pitch and regulation; in Wude, together with Vice Director of the Court for Imperial Sacrifices Zu Xiaosun he received an edict to fix the orthodox sounds of elegant music; Jin investigated ancient facts and compiled one fascicle of 《Orthodox Pitch Modes》, which circulated in his age.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was well versed in pitch and regulation; during Wude, together with Vice Director of the Court for Imperial Sacrifices Zu Xiaosun he received an edict to fix the orthodox sounds of court music; Jin investigated ancient precedents and compiled one fascicle of 《Orthodox Pitch Modes》, which circulated in his day.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：得人者昌，如諸溫儒雅清顯，為一時之稱；

translations.literal: The historiographer says: He who gains men flourishes—as with the various Wen, refined and elegant, clear and eminent, acclaimed in their age;
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer says: A ruler who gains good men flourishes—as with the Wen clan, refined and eminent, acclaimed in their age;

sentences.zh: 叔達才學明辯，中二國之選。

translations.literal: Shuda in talent and learning was clear and argumentative, chosen among the best of two states.
translations.idiomatic: Shuda was gifted in talent and learning and clear in debate, chosen among the best of Chen and Tang.

sentences.zh: 皆抱廊廟之器，俱為社稷之臣。

translations.literal: All bore the capacity for hall and temple, and all were ministers of the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: All bore the capacity for high office, and all served as pillars of the state.

sentences.zh: 威守道，軌臨戎，抗居喪，靜經略，璡音律，仍以懿親，俱至顯位；

translations.literal: Wei kept the Way, Gui faced battle, Kang dwelt in mourning, Jing in strategy, Jin in pitch and regulation—and still as honored kin all reached eminent posts;
translations.idiomatic: Wei kept to the Way, Gui faced battle, Kang excelled in mourning rites, Jing in frontier strategy, Jin in music—and as honored kin all reached eminent posts;

sentences.zh: 才能門第，輝映數朝，豈非得人歟？

translations.literal: talent and lineage shining across several reigns—is this not gaining men?
translations.idiomatic: their talent and lineage shining across several reigns—was this not a matter of gaining the right men?

sentences.zh: 唐之昌也，不亦宜乎！

translations.literal: That Tang flourished—was it not fitting!
translations.idiomatic: That Tang flourished—was it not only fitting!

sentences.zh: 然彥博之褊，竇軌之酷，亦非全器焉。

translations.literal: Yet Yanbo's narrowness and Dou Gui's cruelty show they were not complete vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Yanbo's narrowness and Dou Gui's cruelty show they were not men of complete character.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：溫、陳才位，文蔚典禮。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Wen and Chen in talent and office, Wenwei in canon and ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium says: The Wen and Chen in talent and rank, Wenwei in canon and ritual.

sentences.zh: 諸竇戚裡，榮盛無比。

translations.literal: The various Dou as affinal kin—glory and splendor without compare.
translations.idiomatic: The Dou as imperial affines—glory and splendor without compare.
